gradient

**What this shows** - Chicago crime locations as a heat layer only: no markers, a custom colour gradient and a topographic basemap, filtered by infraction type.

**The SPL**

```spl
| inputlookup chicago-crime.csv | search description=$desc_viz_1$ | eval tooltip=description, coordinates=latitude.",".longitude
```

**How it works**

1. `inputlookup chicago-crime.csv` loads the crime rows (`latitude`, `longitude`, `description`, ...); `search description=$desc_viz_1$` applies the Infraction input.
2. `eval tooltip=description, coordinates=latitude.",".longitude` adds hover text and a combined `coordinates` string.
3. `heatmapEnable=1` sends every row through the heatmap code. No row has a `heatmapLayer`, so all rows go to the default layer `heatmap`, each with the default intensity of 1.
4. `heatmapOnly=1` suppresses all markers, so only the heat is drawn.
5. `heatmapRadius=12.5` and `heatmapColorGradient` (a JSON object of stop to colour; single quotes are accepted) style the layer; `mapTile` picks the basemap.

**Field formats and rules**

| Field | Expected format | Rule / gotcha |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | decimal degrees (number) | Exact lowercase name, from the lookup. Rename `lat`, `lng` and similar before the map. |
| `longitude` | decimal degrees (number) | Exact lowercase name. Rows at 0,0 usually mean missing coordinates. |
| `tooltip` | HTML text | Hover tooltip; not shown while `heatmapOnly=1` because no markers are drawn. |
| `coordinates` | any | Not a reserved Maps+ field: ignored for drawing, passed to drilldown. |
| `heatmapPointIntensity` | number, default 1 | Not set here. Weight per point; normalise to 0-1 when rows are aggregated counts. |

**Try it**

- Set `heatmapOnly` to 0 in the Format panel to see markers on top of the heat.
- Append `, heatmapPointIntensity=if(like(description,"%HANDGUN%"),5,1)` to the `eval` to weight handgun crimes five times more.

> **Studio note:** Studio multiselect inputs ignore the classic `valuePrefix` / `valueSuffix` (`"`) and `delimiter` (` OR `): values are comma-joined with no wrapping, so only the **All** choice (`*`, the default) expands to a valid `description=*` filter. The query text is unchanged. On Maps+ 4.6.9 and earlier, heat layers appear twice in the Studio layer control: untick both entries (fixed in the unreleased 4.6.10). The `heatmapColorGradient` option is passed through unchanged.

**Basemap:** this example uses keyless OpenFreeMap vector tiles (`useOpenFreeMap` = 1). CARTO basemaps need a free API key: see **Help > Basemaps & API keys** for how to get one and where to put it (**Map Tile Override**)." } }, "viz_md_2": { "type": "splunk.markdown", "options": { "markdown": "### Markers plus heat, default gradient

**What this shows** - GPS track points shown as markers with a heat layer underneath, using the default gradient.

**The SPL**

```spl
| inputlookup go_track_trackspoints.csv
```

**How it works**

1. `inputlookup go_track_trackspoints.csv` returns the track points; there is no further processing, since the lookup already has `latitude` and `longitude`.
2. `heatmapEnable=1` runs every row through the heatmap code (default layer `heatmap`, intensity 1), and because `heatmapOnly` is not set, markers are drawn too.
3. `heatmapRadius=12.5` sets the heat radius; the gradient is the option default.
4. `autoFitAndZoom=0` with `mapCenterLat`, `mapCenterLon` and `mapCenterZoom=9` fixes the starting view.

**Field formats and rules**

| Field | Expected format | Rule / gotcha |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | decimal degrees (number) | Exact lowercase name, from the lookup. Rename `lat`, `lng` and similar before the map. |
| `longitude` | decimal degrees (number) | Exact lowercase name. Rows at 0,0 usually mean missing coordinates. |
| `track_id, _time` | any | Not reserved for heat: not drawn, passed to drilldown. (`_time` only matters for paths.) |

**Try it**

- Set `heatmapOnly` to 1 to hide the markers.
- Lower `heatmapRadius` to 6 for tighter hot spots.

> **Studio note:** On Maps+ 4.6.9 and earlier, heat layers appear twice in the Studio layer control: untick both entries (fixed in the unreleased 4.6.10).

**Basemap:** this example uses keyless OpenFreeMap vector tiles (`useOpenFreeMap` = 1). CARTO basemaps need a free API key: see **Help > Basemaps & API keys** for how to get one and where to put it (**Map Tile Override**)." } }, "viz_md_3": { "type": "splunk.markdown", "options": { "markdown": "### Several heat layers, each with its own settings

**How it works**

1. Load `chicago-crime.csv` and filter with `search description=$desc_viz_3$`.
2. `heatmapLayer=case(...)` assigns each row to the layer `vehicle`, `gun` or `default`; Maps+ creates one heat layer per name.
3. `heatmapMinOpacity`, `heatmapBlur`, `heatmapRadius` and `heatmapColorGradient` are set per layer with `case()`. Maps+ reads them from the **first row** of each layer, so every row of a layer should carry the same values (they do here).
4. `heatmapPointIntensity` is the weight per point: 50 for vehicle, 5 for gun and 0.5 for the rest, so vehicle crimes glow hotter.
5. `layerPriority` sets pane order, and `heatmapEnable=1` turns the heat code on.

**Field formats and rules**

| Field | Expected format | Rule / gotcha |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude` | decimal degrees (number) | Exact lowercase name, from the lookup. Rename `lat`, `lng` and similar before the map. |
| `longitude` | decimal degrees (number) | Exact lowercase name. Rows at 0,0 usually mean missing coordinates. |
| `heatmapLayer` | text | Layer name; give every row one, or rows without it fall into the layer `heatmap`. |
| `heatmapMinOpacity, heatmapBlur, heatmapRadius` | numbers as text | Per layer, from the layer's first row; fall back to the panel options. |
| `heatmapColorGradient` | JSON object of stop to colour | Per layer, first row wins. Quotes inside the SPL string are escaped (`\"`); single quotes are also accepted. |
| `heatmapPointIntensity` | number, default 1 | Weight per point. |
| `layerPriority` | integer | Pane order of the layer. |
| `tooltip, coordinates` | text | `tooltip` is the hover text; `coordinates` is not reserved and only passed to drilldown. |

**Try it**

- Add `heatmapInclude="false"` for the `default` rows (in the `eval`) to leave them out of the heat.
